name: philosophy
doc:
PHILOSOPHY - the analytic checks, sealed (issue #11, 2026-10-16: reach, down the domain list). Through
philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY: modal consistency (necessary-and-possible sealed consistent, necessary-but-impossible
sealed INCONSISTENT with claimed false, contingent sealed consistent), the four ethical frameworks on whether they
judge by outcomes, the a priori / a posteriori distinction on Kant's own examples, and Leibniz's law on equal and
unequal property sets. The principles are CITED - the axiom D of modal logic, the taxonomy of ethics, the
identity of indiscernibles and its dispute; the classifications are SEALED. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Philosophy - modality, ethics, knowledge and identity, sealed
sticks.statement: The analytic checks of philosophy are decidable where they are formal: a modal contradiction, a framework's criterion, the source of a claim's warrant, the equality of two property sets.
references: S. Kripke, Semantical considerations on modal logic, Acta Phil. Fennica 16 (1963) 83
I. Kant, Critique of Pure Reason (1781), Introduction - a priori and a posteriori
G. W. Leibniz, Discourse on Metaphysics (1686) section 9; M. Black, The identity of indiscernibles, Mind 61 (1952) 153
J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism (1863); Kant, Groundwork (1785); Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics; Hobbes, Leviathan (1651)

marks.claim: [necessary and possible, SEALED] A claim held necessarily true and possibly true is consistent (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY): what must be, can be. The principle box P implies diamond P is axiom D - valid in every serial frame, so in the systems T, S4 and S5 (the verifier files it under K).

[necessary but impossible, SEALED AS A CONTRADICTION] Necessarily true AND not possibly true is inconsistent - sealed with claimed_consistent = false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY). Box P and not-diamond P cannot both hold: a thing that must be the case cannot also be a thing that cannot be. The engine seals the contradiction as a contradiction.
[contingent, SEALED] Not necessary but possible is consistent (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY): the contingent - true in some worlds, false in others - is where most of what we say lives.
[consequentialism, SEALED] Consequentialism judges an act by its outcomes: true (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY). Mill's greatest happiness is the type.
[deontology, SEALED] Deontology does not: false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY) - the act's conformity to duty is the measure (Kant's categorical imperative), whatever follows.
[virtue ethics, SEALED] Virtue ethics does not: false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY) - the agent's character is the measure (Aristotle).
[contractarianism, SEALED] Contractarianism does not: false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY) - what rational agents would agree to is the measure (Hobbes, Rawls).
[a priori, SEALED] A claim that needs no observation is a priori (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY): Kant's 7 + 5 = 12, known by reason alone.

[a posteriori, SEALED] A claim that needs observation is a posteriori - sealed with claimed_is_a_priori = false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY): that water boils at 100 C at one atmosphere is learned by the thermometer, not the armchair.
[Leibniz's law, SEALED] Two objects with the same properties - red, round, heavy, in any order - are identical under the law (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY): the property SETS are equal.

[and its contrapositive, SEALED] Red, round, heavy against red, round, light: not identical, sealed with claimed false (sealed through philosophy.PHIL_VERIFY). One differing property is enough; the engine names it.

[the principles, CITED] Axiom D (what is necessary is possible), the taxonomy of the four frameworks, Kant's a priori / a posteriori line, and Leibniz's law are PRINCIPLES, cited never sealed. Leibniz's law has two halves: the indiscernibility of identicals (uncontroversial) and the identity of indiscernibles - the half the verifier implements - which Black (1952) disputed with two qualitatively identical spheres. What is sealed is the set comparison; whether sameness of properties IS identity is left as the dispute it is.
marks.source: Kripke (1963); Kant, Critique of Pure Reason, Introduction; Leibniz, Discourse section 9; Black, Mind 61 (1952) 153

marks.claim: [on the one map] Modal logic is propositional logic with two more operators (the formal-logic stick: box and diamond are duals, like and and or under negation). The frameworks are the discernment the mind does (card_floor_the_mind) made explicit. The engine seals what is decidable and declines what is wise: which framework is RIGHT is not a check, and a miss stays a miss.
marks.source: the one map; the formal-logic stick; card_floor_the_mind
